Why is your credit card 22% when the Fed's rate is 4%?

The Fed's own data: card accounts paying interest averaged 22.36% in Q3 2026. The Fed's key rate range tops out at 4% (held on Oct 28, 2026). That's an 18-point gap. Roughly 3.8 points of it is risk: banks wrote off 3.82% of card loans (Q2 2026), because card debt has no house or car behind it. The other 14.5 points or so covers running costs, rewards and the bank's margin. Rough illustration, not an accounting breakdown.

Do you know your card's APR without checking?

Sources: Federal Reserve G.19 and FOMC statement, FRED (fetched Nov 18, 2026). Not financial advice.
